name: Power Distribution Module
summary: Electronic power distribution for the Formula SAE vehicle.
contribution: I designed the schematic and PCB, and guided the firmware logic. Another team member implemented the firmware. The board was manufactured, tested, and installed in the vehicle.
description: The PDM brings high-side switching, current-measurement circuitry, and CAN communication onto a four-layer board. Its copper stack is SIG1 / GND / PWR / SIG2, with the ground and power layers between the outer signal layers.

name: ShieldESP display
summary: An ESP32-based board for the vehicle display.
contribution: I was a main contributor to the display project, working on the ShieldESP hardware and developing the display’s user interface.
description: ShieldESP connects an ESP32 module to the display and the vehicle CAN bus. Separate schematic sheets cover the controller, power supply, and connectors.
facts: Display, touch and SD chip-select signals
note: The images on this page show the PCB. They are not screenshots of the display interface.

name: BSPD
summary: Hardware logic for brake and power plausibility checks.
contribution: I personally designed the BSPD schematic and PCB.
description: The circuit compares the brake and power-related input signals, combines the results using discrete logic, and drives a shutdown relay. The design also includes timing, reset, and protection circuitry.

name: BSS
summary: BMS and insulation-monitor signals connected to the shutdown circuit.
contribution: I reviewed and contributed redesign work to this board as part of the team’s electrical hardware development.
description: The BSS has separate BMS and IMD signal paths. Its schematic includes optocouplers, fault latches, timing circuits, relay outputs, and a reset-switch interface.

name: Precharge
summary: Voltage comparison and relay sequencing for precharge.
contribution: I reviewed and contributed redesign work to the precharge board, including its integration with the vehicle electrical system.
description: The design compares the DC bus voltage with a reference derived from the battery voltage. It uses relay control and delay circuitry to sequence the precharge path and its bypass.
facts: Battery and DC bus voltage dividers
Optocouplers, relay drivers and delay circuitry

name: HV interface board
summary: Vehicle interfaces for high-voltage signals and discharge circuitry.
contribution: I reviewed and contributed redesign work to the HV board as part of the team’s electrical hardware development.
description: This board connects several vehicle electrical functions. The available sheets cover connectors, discharge circuitry, TSLC, and the IR converter circuit.
facts: HV, TSMP, TSAL and vehicle connectors

name: SSI indicator
summary: A red and green LED indicator board with BMS and IMD inputs.
contribution: I contributed to this board as part of the team’s electrical hardware development.
description: The SSI schematic shows red and green LED groups, transistor drive circuits, BMS and IMD panel signals, and a 5 V regulator supplied from 24 V.
